subject: useR tutorial? click data to update inputs?

messages.author: 4818a52a83202bf4
messages.subject: useR tutorial? click data to update inputs?
parts:
Hi ggvis maintainers, I have two questions.

First, would you like to join forces for a useR 2014 tutorial on interactive graphics? There are now many packages for making interactive graphics using R, and I think it would be useful for the community to have a summary of their differences and relative strengths. So far I have heard that the developers of the RIGHT package are also interested, so I was thinking of splitting the 3-hour talk up into 3 sections, with different presenters for each section:

1 hour: simple interactive web graphics (rCharts, googleVis)

1 hour: brushing several linked plots of 1 data.frame (RIGHT, iplots, cranvas)

1 hour: interactive and/or animated graphics (ggvis, animation, animint)

For the last section, I have already started a comparison between the packages:

https://github.com/tdhock/interactive-tutorial/tree/master/animation

It is currently a work in progress, so would you be interested in helping out in the preparation, and/or for presenting the tutorial? The due date for submissions is Jan 5.

Second question: I wanted to reproduce the following interactive visualization using shiny+ggvis:

http://sugiyama-www.cs.titech.ac.jp/~toby/animint/WorldBank/viz.html

So I wrote the following shiny app:

https://github.com/tdhock/interactive-tutorial/tree/master/animation/WorldBank/ggvis

Clicking on the slider changes input$year and clicking the menu changes input$country, but it would also be useful to be able to click on the data points to change those inputs. Is that possible? e.g. clicking a colored circle on the scatterplot changes input$country.

Thanks in advance!

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: useR tutorial? click data to update inputs?
parts:
Hi Toby -

Great idea to have an interactive graphics tutorial at useR! We'd be happy to supply materials and examples for the demo, but I'm not sure it makes sense for us to actually do the presentation -- ggvis is pretty big and complex, so it would only be possible to give a very brief overview if it were part of an hour-long presentation.

Regarding the second question: we're currently working on implementing plot interaction, and clicking is definitely something that we want to support, but it's not there yet. Cool example with the World Bank data!

-Winston

Thanks for your response. I am glad you agree that the tutorial is a good idea, even if you do not want to actually do the presentation. In my current plan I have allocated 15 minutes for each package in the "animation" section, which includes ggvis. I would like to show how to make that World Bank data viz using each of the packages.

One of the main ideas of my tutorial is to highlight the differences and strengths of each package. With that in mind, do you have any ideas about ways to improve the World Bank viz that would highlight the strengths of the ggvis package? If so then I will be sure to mention them in my presentation of ggvis.

messages.author: 4818a52a83202bf4
messages.subject: Re: useR tutorial? click data to update inputs?
parts:
Thanks for the suggestion. I certainly would not want to mischaracterize ggvis.

To clarify, I updated my definition of a "simple interactive graphic" as a "single-layer, single-panel interactive web graphic that can be generated with only 1 line of R code." It seems like making this kind of graphic is a strong point of rCharts and googleVis. For example the multiple time series of the economics data on the rCharts homepage can be produced by

mPlot(x = "date", y = c("psavert", "uempmed"), type = "Line", data = econ)

If ggvis can produce something similar that indeed we should include ggvis in the "simple" section. Actually, I tried to make multiple time series using the examples in ggvis/demo/lines.r, but I just got blank web pages. Could you explain how to make a multiple time series with ggvis?

And actually, if ggvis will do linked brushing, would you be interested in presenting that hour of the tutorial? I also emailed the RIGHT developers to ask about presenting, but Junghoon Lee said that they may be too busy.
